---
title: "Calibrate a count target"
subtitle: "Catalog C-02"
description: "A live TSMM calibrator: choose J and a target for the number of clusters, and the page solves Gamma(a, b) at once, or says why it cannot."
toc: false
---

State what you expect about the number of clusters K_J among your J units, as a mean and a
variance (or a variance inflation factor, VIF: sigma^2 = VIF (mu_K − 1)). The calibrator
finds the Gamma(a, b) hyperprior on alpha whose implied K_J has exactly that mean and
variance.

```{=html}
<div id="w-cal" class="dpx-host column-page"></div>
<script src="../../js/vendor/d3.min.js"></script>
<script src="../../js/vendor/plot.min.js"></script>
<script src="../../js/bundles/tsmm-calibrator.js"></script>
<script>
  (function () {
    var q = new URLSearchParams(location.search), spec = {};
    ["J", "mu", "var"].forEach(function (k) { var v = q.get(k); if (v !== null && v !== "" && isFinite(+v)) spec[k] = +v; });
    if (q.get("preset")) spec.preset = q.get("preset");
    window.__dpxCal = DPX["tsmm-calibrator"].mountWidget(document.getElementById("w-cal"), spec);
  })();
</script>
```

- **The J = 50 example.** "About 5 clusters", with VIF 2.5 (sigma^2 = 10), gives
  Gamma(1.4082, 1.0770) after five Newton steps from the closed-form start (2.667, 2.608).
- **The applications.** STAR (J = 79, "between 2 and 8 with 80% probability", sigma^2 = 5.48)
  gives Gamma(5.134, 4.939); Table 2 of the paper (J = 100, VIF 2.5) gives Gamma(1.666,
  1.646).
- **When there is no answer.** "Between 3 and 10 with 95% probability" at J = 100 asks for
  a variance of 3.19 around a mean of 6.5, but no Gamma prior with that mean has a variance
  below 4.52. The calibrator says so instead of returning a poor fit. A variance at or above
  (mu_K − 1)(J − mu_K) is refused too: no count on 1..J with that mean can reach it.
- **Just above the bound.** A target a little above the smallest variance still has an exact
  answer, with a very large shape a: the prior is nearly a point mass (CV(alpha) below .01).
  The calibrator shows the mean and variance it achieves beside the target; a result that
  misses the target by more than 10^-6 is labelled approximate, never calibrated.
  Try `?J=50&mu=5&var=3.2219`.
- The weights come along unasked: check Pr(W_SB > .5) in the read-out, and see
  [the J = 50 worked example](worked-example-j50.qmd) for what to do when it is too high.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
Solved by dp-core `tsmmFit` in the browser; checked against DPprior 2.0.0 on
[the parity page](tsmm-parity.qmd). K_J is the number of fitted components among the J units.
:::

Standalone version: [embed/tsmm-calibrator.html](../../embed/tsmm-calibrator.html)
(for example `?J=79&mu=5&var=5.48`).
